'''Wayne Velicer''' (March 4, 1944 – October 15, 2017) was an American psychologist known for his research in [[quantitative psychology|quantitative]] and [[health psychology]]. He taught at the [[University of Rhode Island]] from 1973 until his death in 2017. He worked with [[James O. Prochaska]] to help to found the University of Rhode Island's Cancer Prevention Research Center, of which he subsequently served as co-director.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Harlow |first1=Lisa L. |last2=Aiken |first2=Leona |last3=Blankson |first3=A. Nayena |last4=Boodoo |first4=Gwyneth M. |last5=Brick |first5=Leslie Ann D. |last6=Collins |first6=Linda M. |last7=Cumming |first7=Geoff |last8=Fava |first8=Joseph L. |last9=Goodwin |first9=Matthew S. |last10=Hoeppner |first10=Bettina B. |last11=MacKinnon |first11=David P. |date=2021-05-04 |title=A Tribute to the Mind, Methodology and Mentoring of Wayne Velicer |journal=Multivariate Behavioral Research |language=en |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=377–389 |doi=10.1080/00273171.2020.1729083 |issn=0027-3171 |pmc=7438240 |pmid=32077317}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-12-05 |title=URI loses a 'giant' in his field, in the classroom, in life |url=https://web.uri.edu/chs/2017/12/05/uri-loses-a-giant-in-his-field-in-the-classroom-in-life/ |access-date=2022-01-08 |website=University of Rhode Island |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
In 2004, Velicer was one of six University of Rhode Island faculty to be named an [[ISI Highly Cited Researcher]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-03-10 |title=Six at URI among world's most highly cited researchers |url=https://www.uri.edu/news/2004/03/six-at-uri-among-worlds-most-highly-cited-researchers/ |access-date=2022-01-08 |website=University of Rhode Island |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2013, he received the [[Samuel J. Messick]] Distinguished Scientific Contributions Award from Division 5 of the [[American Psychological Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-02-20 |title=URI psychology professors recognized for national success in their fields |url=https://www.uri.edu/news/2013/02/uri-psychology-professors-recognized-for-national-success-in-their-fields/ |access-date=2022-01-08 |website=University of Rhode Island |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2018, he was posthumously inducted into the University of Rhode Island's Lifetime Service Society.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-16 |title=URI inducts 13 to Lifetime Service Society |url=https://www.uri.edu/news/2018/10/uri-inducts-13-to-lifetime-service-society/ |access-date=2022-01-08 |website=University of Rhode Island |language=en-US}}</ref>
